#3055. Here's How Much a $5,000 Investment in SpaceX Stock Could Be Worth by November 2027

Space Exploration Technologies' stock price could be noticeably higher by this time next year, but successful investing requires thinking about the long term.

Analysts' 12-month price targets aren't guarantees of where a stock could trade down the road. But with a company like Space Exploration Technologies (SPCX +0.72%), price targets can help retail investors establish a risk-to-reward framework to inform their investment considerations.

After all, with SpaceX not only involved in the space sector but also viewing its biggest opportunities in artificial intelligence (AI), it helps to get a ballpark sense of what an investment today could be worth a year from now.

Today, we'll look at how analysts are valuing the company to get an idea of how much a $5,000 investment made now could be worth by November 2027.

According to data tracked by CNN, analysts generally have a favorable outlook on SpaceX. Out of the 47 who cover the stock, 77% rate it a buy, 19% a hold, and 4% a sell.

Among that group, the median one-year price target is $245, which would be an 82.4% gain from the Nov. 6 closing price of $134.27. We'll ignore the highest target of $800, as SpaceX is unlikely to reach that in just a year. We will, however, focus on the lowest target, $118, which would amount to a 12.1% loss.

If someone bought $5,000 worth of SpaceX at the Nov. 6 closing price of $134.27, that would yield approximately 37 shares. With 37 shares, if SpaceX reached the median one-year price target of $245 per share, that $5,000 investment would be worth $9,065. If the stock price sank to the lowest target, $118, that $5,000 investment would be worth $4,336.

SpaceX is showing accelerated revenue growth, as evidenced by its third-quarter results, with sales growing 161% to $14.5 billion. The company also reported net income of $4.4 billion, a nice change of pace from the $1 billion net loss it reported in the prior-year period.

The company is enjoying a noticeable sales growth trajectory. It's forecasting first-quarter 2027 revenue of between $33 billion and $37 billion, which is impressive given that it reported $18.6 billion in revenue for all of 2025.

If SpaceX can keep growing its sales and trimming its net losses, investor enthusiasm could provide some fuel to help the stock price reach that $245 target.

There are a few reasons why SpaceX's stock price could fall to $118, and it could always slide even further. One of the factors putting pressure on it now is the recent broad sell-off in AI stocks. While SpaceX's AI segment went from generating $813 million in the third quarter of 2025 to $7.5 billion in the third quarter of 2026, it's still spending heavily to build its data center infrastructure. Its capital expenditures totaled $19.6 billion in the third quarter, with $16.4 billion of that spent on its AI division alone.

The share price could also fall amid a broad market sell-off or due to a few underwhelming quarterly performances.

The risk-to-reward framework looks favorable over the next year, but doesn't make SpaceX an automatic investment just based on one-year price targets. Ultimately, meaningful wealth isn't typically created after just one year of owning a stock, and it will take years for SpaceX to execute on its ambitions.

Even in this stock's short trading history, there have been many wild price swings. Those are only likely to continue. To hold onto this stock through the rockiest moments requires shareholders to have strong conviction in the company. While it's common to hear people talk in retrospect about how much money retail investors could have made by investing in one of CEO Elon Musk's other companies, Tesla, in its early days, what is less often shared are the tales of investors who sold their stock along the way because they couldn't handle the volatility.

With SpaceX, capturing the biggest gains will require patience and a strong enough belief in the company that a shareholder won't react with a knee-jerk sell if they see the stock price head significantly lower.

#3052. MasterCraft (MCFT) Q1 2027 Earnings Call Transcript

Legacy margins climbed as Chaparral and Robalo integration advanced.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

MasterCraft Boat Holdings, Inc. (MCFT -3.17%) reported financial results for the first quarter of its six-month transition period, highlighting the strategic integration of the Marine Products acquisition. Management reported that the addition of the Chaparral and Robalo brands has diversified the portfolio across price points and categories, reducing dependence on any single boating segment. The company reported significant margin expansion in its legacy business, driven by a premium product mix and operational cost discipline. Management indicated that dealer health remains a priority, with inventory levels currently below prior-year levels. The company raised its guidance for the transition period based on first quarter performance and continued synergy execution.

Operator: Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for standing by, and welcome to the MasterCraft Boat Holdings, Inc. First Quarter 2026 Transition Period Earnings Conference Call. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded. [Operator Instructions] I would now like to hand the conference over to your speaker today, Alec Harmon, Senior Director, Strategy and Investor Relations. Please go ahead, sir.

Alec Harmon: Thank you, operator, and welcome, everyone. Thank you for joining us today as we discuss the first quarter transition period performance of MasterCraft Boat Holdings. As a reminder, today's call is being webcast live and will also be archived on our website for 1 year for future listening. With me on this morning's call is Brad Nelson, Chief Executive Officer; and Scott Kent, Chief Financial Officer. Brad will begin with an overview of our operational performance. After that, Scott will discuss our financial performance. Brad will then offer some closing remarks before we open the call for questions.

Before we begin, we would like to remind participants that the information contained in this call is current only as of today, November 10, 2026. The company assumes no obligation to update any statements, including forward-looking statements. Statements that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and subject to the safe harbor disclaimer in today's press release. Additionally, on this call, we will discuss non-GAAP measures that include or exclude items not indicative of our ongoing operations. For each non-GAAP measure, we will also provide the most directly comparable GAAP measure in today's press release, which includes a reconciliation of these non-GAAP measures to our GAAP results.

Beginning this quarter, certain corporate costs that were previously reported within our Performance and Wake segment are now being reported separately. This change better reflects how we manage the combined company, affecting segment presentation only and has no impact on our consolidated results. Prior period segment results have also been recast for comparability. Also as a reminder, in connection with our change to a December 31 fiscal year-end, today's results cover the first 3 months of our 6-month transition period, which runs from July 1 through December 31, 2026. We will compare these results to the prior year period, which includes the 3 months ended September 28, 2025.

Because this quarter includes a full quarter of contribution from Chaparral and Robalo and the prior year period includes no contribution from these brands, we will speak to our results on both a total company basis and a Legacy basis, with Legacy representing our Performance and Wake segment, including corporate costs, and our Leisure segment. Unless otherwise noted, the following commentary is made on a continuing operations basis, and all references to specific quarters and periods will be on a fiscal basis. With that, I will turn the call over to Brad.

Bradley Nelson: Thank you, Alec, and good morning, everyone. We delivered results above our expectations in the first quarter of the transition period. In our first full quarter operating as a combined company following the acquisition of Marine Products, we exceeded expectations for both net sales and adjusted EBITDA with strong Legacy execution complemented by the first full quarter contribution from Chaparral and Robalo. Total company net sales grew more than 120% year-over-year. Importantly, our Legacy business net sales grew 37% and delivered adjusted EBITDA growth of nearly 140%. We are pleased with our performance this quarter. These results reflect deliberate product, commercial and operational actions we have taken across our business to drive premium mix, clean channels and reduce costs.

These efforts are foundational and continue to build on the momentum we have delivered over the past several quarters. Dealer health remains strong and continues to be a priority for MCBH. Dealer inventories across our established brands are healthy and below prior year levels with inventory turns better than last year and near pre-COVID levels as we exit the quarter. Because of this, we believe our dealers have more flexibility to respond to market demand while we remain disciplined in aligning wholesale shipments with retail demand. Now turning to retail. On a calendar year-to-date basis, total company retail continues to outperform the broader market. Consumer sentiment remains cautious, and we are monitoring retail trends closely as we plan production.

Against that backdrop, with the recent addition of the Chaparral and Robalo brands, the benefit from diversification of our portfolio is proving to be helpful, providing exposure across a broader range of consumers, product categories and price points. Chaparral and Robalo performed particularly well at retail during the quarter. That broader coverage gives us more ways to serve customers and reduces our dependence on any single boating category or market. Looking ahead, we believe the breadth of our portfolio, combined with our continued focus on product innovation, positions us well to continue our momentum.

We have an exciting pipeline of new products in development across our brands that we believe will further strengthen our competitive advantages and provide additional opportunities for growth. Our approach and priorities remain steady. We will continue aligning wholesale with retail demand to preserve dealer health, leveraging our flexible operating model to control costs and investing in innovation and synergies throughout the cycle. Now turning to our segments. In Performance and Wake, MasterCraft continues to lead in the premium ski/wake category. Our model year 2027 lineup builds on the momentum of the next-generation X Series with enhancements designed around the driver and rider experience.

The success of the next-generation X Series is a clear example of the strength of our products and portfolio strategy and our ability to translate a deep understanding of our consumers into products that resonate in the market. Combined with our ongoing cost, productivity and quality initiatives, those actions are driving stronger earnings and margin performance. Together, these factors contributed to a strong Q1 performance with MasterCraft delivering a 26.7% adjusted EBITDA margin, generating $21.8 million of adjusted EBITDA. The strength of these results are evidence of the earnings progress created by innovation, simplification and sustained operational execution.

During the quarter, MasterCraft also made its first appearance at the Monaco Yacht Show, where we showcased the X24 as a superyacht tender featuring custom factory-installed lifting points, expanding MasterCraft's presence within the ultra-premium boating market and continuing to expand the brand globally with luxury customers. In Leisure, adjusted EBITDA margin improved nearly 500 basis points year-over-year, driven by higher volumes, lower discounts and cost initiatives. For model year 2027, Crest expanded its Conquest SE lineup at an accessible price point and refreshed the Caribbean Series, including the new 22-foot model, while both Crest and Balise now offer twin-engine configurations on 24- and 26-foot models.

Balise also broadened its addressable market with a 22-foot model across all layouts and an all-new entertainer layout featuring a wet bar, refrigerator and grill. We are also building real momentum in distribution. Crest and Balise added a meaningful number of new dealers during the quarter, including several existing partners from across the broader MCBH network. This reflects the value of our broader brand portfolio and the opportunity to deepen relationships with high-quality dealers across categories. Expanded sales coverage, a focused dealer acquisition strategy and an enhanced product lineup, all position our Leisure brands well for growth as conditions improve. Turning to Recreation and Sport Fishing segment.

We are pleased with our integration progress as we continue to advance operations as a combined company. Our focus on synergies has shifted from planning to execution with initiatives underway and dedicated teams in place across product and portfolio strategy, distribution expansion, operating disciplines and sourcing. On sourcing, our corporate sourcing team is beginning to realize the benefits from the increased scale of the combined company while continuing to identify additional opportunities across our supplier base. Operationally, we are also taking steps to optimize our manufacturing footprint, improve capacity utilization and reduce costs. These are foundational steps in building a more efficient and profitable combined company.

And while we remain early in the process, we are encouraged by the progress to date and the opportunities we see ahead. Turning to capital allocation. Our priorities remain unchanged, maintaining a strong balance sheet, investing in innovation and growth, which includes synergies, returning capital to shareholders through share repurchases and maintaining a disciplined approach to M&A. Overall, we executed well in a dynamic market, exceeded our expectations and advanced the integration of our combined portfolio. With that, I'll turn the call over to Scott.

Scott Kent: Thanks, Brad, and good morning, everyone. I'll start by reviewing our results for the first quarter, then cover our balance sheet and capital allocation and finish with our outlook for the remainder of the transition period. Net sales for the quarter were $154.1 million, an increase of 123.4% compared to the prior year period, including $59.3 million from our Recreation and Sport Fishing segment. On a Legacy basis, net sales were $94.8 million, an increase of 37.4% compared to $69 million in the prior year period, driven by higher volumes of our next-generation X Series models, which drove favorable mix, along with disciplined pricing and lower discounts.

Consolidated gross margin was 21.1% compared to 22.3% in the prior year period, reflecting the blended margin profile following the Marine Products acquisition. Legacy gross margins expanded 600 basis points to 28.3% from 22.3% in the prior year period, driven by improved fixed cost absorption, favorable mix, lower discounts and operating improvements across both our Performance and Wake, and Leisure segments. Operating expenses were $20.5 million compared to $11.6 million in the prior year period. The increase primarily reflects a full quarter of Recreation and Sport Fishing as well as additional acquisition and integration costs related to the Marine Products transaction.

Adjusted net income was $12.2 million or $0.50 per diluted share compared to $4.7 million or $0.29 per diluted share in the prior year period. Adjusted EBITDA was $20.1 million with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 13% compared to $7 million and 10.1% in the prior year period. On a Legacy basis, adjusted EBITDA was $16.7 million, with margin expanding 750 basis points to 17.6%. As a reminder on the purchase accounting, our adjusted results this quarter exclude $1.9 million of integration and transaction-related expenses, $0.6 million of amortization of acquired intangibles and the remaining $0.3 million of inventory step-up related to the Marine Products combination, which is now fully recognized.

Consistent with what we outlined last quarter, intangible amortization and depreciation for the acquired company are now running at normalized levels of approximately $0.6 million and $2.6 million per quarter, respectively. Turning to the balance sheet. We generated $2.9 million of free cash flow in the quarter and ended the period with $41.9 million in cash, no debt and full availability under our $75 million revolving credit facility for total liquidity of $116.9 million. After pausing share repurchases while completing the Marine Products acquisition, we resumed buybacks in the quarter, consistent with our long-standing approach to capital allocation. We repurchased approximately $4.8 million of our shares with approximately $18.7 million remaining under our current authorization.

With a strong balance sheet and cash generation, share repurchases remain an important part of our capital allocation strategy. Now turning to our outlook. Based on our first quarter out-performance and current expectation, we are raising our guidance for the 6-month transition period. We now expect net sales of between $293 million and $297 million, adjusted EBITDA of between $32 million and $34 million and adjusted earnings per share of between $0.75 and $0.80. We continue to expect capital expenditures of approximately $9 million for the period. Our priorities for the remainder of the period remain unchanged, aligning wholesale with retail demand, protecting dealer health, maintaining cost discipline and executing our synergy plan.

We believe this disciplined approach positions us well to navigate the current environment while continuing to strengthen the business for the long term. As we look to the December quarter, we expect our underlying build rates and AUSPs to remain consistent with Q1. However, normal holiday seasonality will likely result in modestly lower sequential shipments due to fewer production days. Overall, we remain confident in the strength of our portfolio, our balance sheet and the long-term earnings power of the combined company. This quarter's performance demonstrates another step forward with strong execution, disciplined cost management and commercial optimization. Our financial flexibility will allow us to continue investing in innovation while also aggressively pursuing our synergy plan.

As we continue executing our focused plan and leveraging the scale of the combined company, we believe we have a meaningful opportunity for ongoing value creation. With that, I'll turn it back to Brad for closing remarks.

Bradley Nelson: Thanks, Scott. This quarter reinforces three important drivers of our long-term earnings potential. First, commercial and operational execution across our business is translating into higher earnings. Second, our expanded brand portfolio and growing dealer network are creating new opportunities for growth across categories and end markets. And third, the investments we are making to capture synergies and leverage the scale and capabilities of the combined company provide meaningful opportunities that we believe will drive further value creation. Looking ahead, our priorities remain clear. We will continue to align wholesale with retail demand, drive operational improvements and invest in product innovation that supports the long-term competitive strength of our brands. We are moving decisively from synergy planning to execution.

Our focus is on preserving what makes each of our brands unique and successful while unlocking opportunities created by the scale and capabilities of the combined company. With a strong balance sheet, a flexible operating model and five leading brands, we are confident in our ability to execute through the current environment while building an even stronger company for the long term. I want to thank our team members, dealer partners, suppliers and shareholders for their continued support and another strong quarter. Operator, you may now open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Your first question comes from Joe Altobello with Raymond James.

Joseph Altobello: First question on the guidance. You obviously raised the transition period guidance, but it seems like the September quarter was better than you originally thought and the December quarter, maybe a tad lighter than you originally thought. Were there any timing issues in the quarter? Are you seeing any margin pressures cropping up here in the December quarter?

Scott Kent: Yes, Joe, I think our -- we really outperformed a little bit in the first quarter, and some of that was timing. So we did shift a bit of our production from Q2 into Q1 or just shipped a few of it a little early. So that's a lot of it. Remember, December -- the December quarter does have some less production days in it because of the normal holiday seasonality. So it is a little lower from a quarter sequential basis. But the underlying build rates and really the ASPs and all that are consistent with Q1. So it's just a matter of some timing fluctuations between costs as well as build rates between the quarters.

Joseph Altobello: Okay. Perfect. And you sort of addressed this a little bit in your prepared remarks, but how would you assess the promotional environment in the ski/wake category at this point?

Scott Kent: Generally, I think we're -- it's still a competitive environment out there. We're still having to do discounts. We think they're pretty much more normalized to some degree. There is a cleaner channels out there from our perspective, and that does help us to keep our discounts low. Our new products that we've been introducing, especially around the XStar and the X Series product line have also helped us not have to do a lot of discounting. So a lot of the actions we've been taking really over the last 2 years are really helping us keep those discounts a little lower than what we might have to do if our channels are a little more unhealthy.

Joseph Altobello: Are you being forced at all to sort of counter other manufacturers' discounts?

Scott Kent: Again, discounts are probably a little higher, but not anything beyond what we'd call normal. We're generally doing our discounts in the normal times we do discounts. So again, we think our position with our dealer health as well as our channel and product are really helping us keep our discounts a little lower.

Operator: Your next question comes from Anna Glaessgen with B. Riley Securities.

Anna Glaessgen: I'd like to start with that gross margin number you gave us on the Legacy business, 28.3%, pretty impressive considering the historical performance, a number we haven't seen in quite some years. Maybe give us some perspective on how this was achieved despite still at a lower production rate than historical norms and to what extent there was maybe anything onetime in there?

Scott Kent: Again, the Legacy gross margin did expand about 600 basis points to the 28.3% that you mentioned. It does reflect some improved absorption year-over-year on that increased volumes. It does have favorable mix. Again, our X Series product that is driving a bit extra sales in the quarter from what X Series would typically do because of the success of that product. We do have some lower discounts on a year-over-year basis. And we do continue to have continued operating improvements, not just in our MasterCraft division, but also in our Leisure segment and our Pontoon brands as well.

So again, all of our strong pipeline management, the new products and operating execution has really been transferring into profitability and showing just the kind of power that we can have when we actually are able to grow sales.

Anna Glaessgen: Got it. And then coming back to retail, are we still expecting for the overall transition period for units to decline in the 5% to 10% range?

Bradley Nelson: Yes, Anna, this is Brad. It's clearly a selective market out there. Consumers remain cautious. But yes, consistent with our prior view, our guidance assumes market down for this calendar year period to be roughly down between the 5% to 10% that we mentioned prior. And then going forward, we're planning for a continued cautious market, but there are buyers out there. It's just the market is not broken. It's just more selective. And in recent periods of time, we continue to be rewarded just with good execution on product as well as a clean channel, and we'll continue to align production of retail to -- of wholesale to retail.

Operator: Your next question comes from Gregory Miller with Truist Securities.

Gregory Miller: For my first question, I'd like to get your perspective on how initial boat shows have proceeded, including the FLIBS recently. I appreciate there's weather in Fort Lauderdale. But outside of that, I'd be curious to get your impressions on your brand's performance there.

Bradley Nelson: Greg, yes, the read on FLIBS and just some of the early sentiment out there across the industry and the sectors within the industry and our categories have been pretty much flattish year-over-year. There's a couple of exceptions to that rule, maybe some strengths and weaknesses. But in general, we've seen -- our performance at both shows has been consistent with that with the broader marine category, which is flattish. In a couple of categories, we've seen better performance. But it seems like attendance at the show was down a little bit, but at the same time, there were still active buyers engaged. So the quality of the buyers seemed slightly improved.

Scott Kent: I remember that the FLIBS show -- you might remember that the FLIBS show is really a saltwater show as well as a bigger boat show. So our brands are not quite as fully represented at the FLIBS show. Really, it's our Robalo brand mostly that is at that show and has the more significant presence. So being flattish on Robalo was actually pretty positive for us.

Gregory Miller: Great. For my follow-up, you mentioned on the call and then you had the press release before earnings on the dealer network expansion, which is a pretty significant number of dealer additions coming from your Legacy brands. So I was just hoping to get a little more context in terms of how that all came to pass in the last couple of months. And then in particular, any thoughts on further growth internationally?

Bradley Nelson: Yes. Distribution in general and a strong dealer network, that's a growth lever for us long stated. It's part of our core strategy. So we always work on that, and we'll continue. Now with the addition of Chaparral and Robalo, we have a boat for everybody. We've got a wide range of price points. We have a diversity of categories. We're not as reliant on a category or two within Marine. So that certainly helps us. So we were able to add dealers in the past quarter in all of our brands. And some of those were international, but most of those were in North America. And some of them were cross-brand polymerization within our MCBH family.

There are active discussions happening. We already signed some of those and already seeing some boats move accordingly. But there are ongoing discussions, numerous, in fact, between our newly expanded dealer network going forward, and we see strong potential as that unfolds. Ultimately, our broader portfolio gives our dealers much more flexibility through this dynamic market environment, and it just gives us a lot more ways to win, and we're starting to see that.

Operator: Your next question comes from Noah Zatzkin with KeyBanc Capital Markets.

Noah Zatzkin: I guess maybe if you could expand a bit on kind of like what were you're tracking in regards to the synergy opportunities around Chaparral and Robalo. Just some context about kind of where you're tracking a plan and the opportunity that remains ahead.

Bradley Nelson: Yes. We've got -- we've already captured approximately $6 million of annual public company and overhead savings from the transaction. We are now moving from a broader synergy and integration perspective, we're pleased with our progress. It's on pace. We're moving now from planning into execution. We do have dedicated teams working initiatives around sourcing, operating initiatives, footprint, portfolio as well as distribution initiatives. And we're seeing some early sourcing benefits starting to emerge. So that will continue to mature with time. Some of these things will take a little bit more time, and we look forward to giving updates as visibility improves in the future.

Scott Kent: And I'd generally say we're on track, if not ahead, in some of our synergy plans versus what we laid out. So I think we're really pleased with the progress so far.

Noah Zatzkin: And hoping you could maybe just comment on what you're seeing or hearing in terms of kind of health of the broader industry dealer base now out of selling season.

Scott Kent: As we talk to our financing partners, generally speaking, I'd say industry inventories are down across the board. Dealer health is generally healthy across. That doesn't mean you don't have the occasional problem with a dealer here and there, but certainly nothing broad-based that's certainly causing any overall concerns at the moment.

Bradley Nelson: Well, I would add, in general, with the inventory side of that, Noah, managing pipeline inventory, as you probably know, is central to how we manage this business. So managing that pipeline, we feel good about the number of units that are out there as well, we feel generally good about the aging profile of those units. And that's going to help us. Dealers right now seem fine. It's one of the stronger parts of our story actually as we lean forward as they now have flexibility to deal with a dynamic consumer.

Operator: Your next question comes from Gerrick Johnson with Seaport Research Partners.

Gerrick Johnson: I'm interested in Crest and the expansion of distribution there. Pontoons are obviously very competitive and you have a few new competitors coming into the space. So it looks like you added 13 dealers. How much of that came from the MPX relationship? And if it was organic, what is it about Crest that's enticing dealers to take on the brand?

Bradley Nelson: Yes, Gerrick. Overall, let me make a broader statement around Leisure. Team is really engaged, a strong team, making progress, moving in the right direction. That business, just from a broader perspective, margins up nearly 500 bps. It's now 6 consecutive quarters of profit growth due to cost initiatives and efficiency initiatives. So we're pleased with the progress. It's not fully where it needs to be, but key to that effort is distribution expansion that you've mentioned. Finding dealers that are truly aligned with our product innovation and with the market right now is core. So among those that we signed, yes, some of those are due to MCBH relationships across, including Chaparral and Robalo and we're early.

So we're pleased with the early progress there. It has strong potential. As you know, some of those things take time to unfold to get a dealer on board, to get them signed, to get them engaged on the product, trained, develop to where they can take a healthy stocking position and then start retailing boats. We're making progress on all those fronts, but it's still early. And that's really what we're seeing with dealers is interest in the product refreshes that we've done. So we've expanded our Conquest lineup, our SE lineup, which adds a variety of new affordable price points.

The team has refreshed the Caribbean series, added twin configuration -- twin engine configurations on all of our 24- and 26-foot models for both Crest and Balise and a brand-new Balise 22-footer across layouts. So we're seeing dealers engaged on products, on our innovation stance, some of the structural changes we made in the business and then the quality of the products remains high. We're pleased with the data that we're seeing there, too.

Gerrick Johnson: Okay. Great. Sounds good. And then on Robalo and Chaparral, you're kind of more of a midrange kind of boat brands there. That's kind of the cohort of consumers that are feeling the most pressure. So what's going on there to drive the outperformance versus the industry for both Robalo and Chaparral?

Bradley Nelson: Well, you've got two proud brands that have been -- Chaparral obviously being a market leader in the Gen-Rec and runabout space continues to be that. Tremendous dealer network, tried and true proven products, proven execution, high-quality boats. And with Robalo on the saltfish and sportfish side of the house, is surging. We're pleased with market share gains there and a very engaged dealer network. And we're seeing some continued vibrancy in that sport fish market. It's one of the more resilient categories within Marine. And our price point diversity now across those boats, it's not all midrange. We've got price points from low to premium, and that diversification across all of our brands is helping us right now.

We've been pleased with the early progress.

Scott Kent: I think some of the product that we've introduced with especially the Robalo has also been really strong. They've got a really strong dual console lineup with a couple of new entrants in the dual console lines. They've also added some additional center consoles. They also have a Bay Boat series. And frankly, we've been winning share in all 3 of the segments that we compete in with some of the product introductions that we've been introducing with that lineup as well. So Robalo has really been a shining star for us from a market share perspective.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. This concludes today's call. Thank you for attending. You may now disconnect.

#3046. Grupo Cibest (CIB) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Nequi's spinoff is complete and its loan book is expanding fast.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Grupo Cibest S.A. (CIB -3.96%) reported third quarter results that included loan growth acceleration and the completion of the Nequi spinoff. Management stated that commercial lending served as the primary driver of portfolio expansion as demand for new projects in Colombia increased. The company revised its full-year loan growth guidance upward to reflect this stronger demand. The transition of Nequi into an independent commercial financing company was completed on Sept. 1, and the entity now serves 29 million customers. Management indicated that capital allocation strategies, including the divestment of Banistmo and new capital instrument issuances, are intended to optimize the group's structure for long-term returns.

Operator: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the Grupo Cibest Bancolombia Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. My name is Carrie, and I will be your operator for today's call. [Operator Instructions] Please note that this conference is being recorded. Please note that this conference call will include forward-looking statements, including statements related to our future performance, capital position, credit-related expenses and credit losses. All forward-looking statements, whether made in this conference call and future filings in press releases or verbal address matters that involve risks and uncertainties.

Consequently, there are factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from those indicated in such statements, including exchanges in general economic and business conditions, changes in currency exchange rates and interest rates, introductions of competing products by other companies, lack of acceptance of new products or services by our targeted clients, changes in business strategy and various other factors that we describe in our reports filed with the SEC. With us today is Mr. Juan Carlos Mora, Chief Executive Officer; Mr. Mauricio Botero Wolff, Chief Strategy and Financial Officer; and Ms. Laura Clavijo, Chief Economist. I will now turn the call over to Mr. Juan Carlos Mora, Chief Executive Officer. Mr. Juan Carlos, you may begin.

Juan Uribe: Good morning, and thank you for joining Grupo Cibest's Third Quarter Conference Call. Please turn to Slide 2. In the third quarter, Colombia faced a difficult political, social and economic environment. A tense government transition was followed by a major earthquake in the Southwest. This increased fiscal concern and raise questions about how quickly and on what scale, reconstruction can restore infrastructure, economic activity and community well-being. Overall, we now expect the economy to have grown 2.1% in the third quarter, below earlier forecasts. Laura Clavijo will elaborate on this shortly. Even so, we delivered strong results.

Credit origination rebound sharply, led by commercial loans as confidence grew in the rule of law and security and as expectations rose for a credible path to fiscal adjustment. Net income reached COP 2 trillion in the quarter. Year-to-date, it is up 10.5%, more than offsetting Banistmo's contribution last year. NIM ended the quarter at 7.4%. The Investment income stabilized, time deposits resumed growth and lower spread commercial loans led the expansion on the loan book. Cost of risk rose 1.9% on higher consumer provisions. This was as expected and within our guided range. The strict expense discipline also underpinned solid operating performance. As a result, ROE for the quarter stood at 21.7%.

On September 1, we reached another corporate milestone. Separation of Nequi from Bancolombia. Nequi is Colombia's leading neo bank with a growing presence in Central America. It is now an independent commercial financing company, wholly owned by Grupo Cibest. This spinoff is designed to accelerate its development as a leading regional neo bank. In July, we also completed a intra-Group additional Tier 1 capital instrument transaction to further optimize Bancolombia's capital structure. I will now turn the call over to our Chief Economist, Laura Clavijo for an overview of the macroeconomic landscape. Laura?

Laura Clavijo: Thank you, Juan Carlos. If you could please proceed to Slide 4. Turning to Colombia, the economy enters 2027 with a mixed but gradually improving outlook. Our central view is that the year will be characterized by two competing forces, an improving investment cycle and post-earthquake reconstruction on the one hand and the necessary adjustment in fiscal and monetary conditions on the other. We expect GDP growth to moderate from 2.6% in 2026 to 2.4% in 2027. Household consumption should remain an important source of growth, but lose momentum as high interest rates, persistent inflation and softer labor market conditions constrained disposable income. At the same time, fiscal consolidation will reduce the contribution from government spending.

Encouragingly, the composition of growth should become more investment-oriented. This investment is projected to rise above 17% of GDP, supported by construction, mining and energy projects as well as reconstruction following the August earthquake. Inflation remains one of the key challenges, following a projected 6.7% year-end reading in 2026, headline inflation could peak at 7.3% during the first half of 2027, largely reflecting the impact of El Niño on food and regulated prices, together with indexation and the minimum wage adjustments. We expect these supply side pressures to fade during the second half, bringing inflation down to 5.5% by December. Nevertheless, still well above the Central Bank's target range. This inflation backdrop will keep monetary conditions tight.

We suspect the policy rate could rise further to 12.5% and remain at this level well into 2027 with the Central Bank waiting for clear evidence of disinflation before restarting the easing cycle. We, therefore, anticipate only modest cuts in the fourth quarter while fiscal risks and elevated global rates further constrained the scope for monetary easing. The fiscal position remains the main macroeconomic vulnerability. An ambitious economic rescue bill worth 2.4% of GDP, containing a significant budget cut and additional taxes are being discussed in Congress before year-end. The signals of fiscal responsibility but be weighed against significant expenditure rigidities and historically high financing requirements.

Our baseline scenario speaks of a Central Government deficit of 7.9% of GDP in 2027, compared with 7.2% in 2026 and assumes a fiscal adjustment of at least 1.5% of GDP to maintain investor confidence and set the path towards fiscal sustainability. Finally, external accounts remain manageable, although the current account deficit is expected to widen from 2.5% of GDP in 2026 to 3.2% in 2027. Importantly, remittances of around 3.4% of GDP should remain an important buffer, keeping the external deficit below its historical average of approximately 4%. Overall, 2027 should be viewed less of a year of acceleration and more of a year of transition.

Growth remains resilient, and its composition improves but Colombia will need to navigate sticky inflation, restrictive financial conditions and above all, a demanding fiscal adjustment before a more balanced and sustainable expansion can take hold. If you could please proceed to Slide 5. Turning to Central America. The outlook for El Salvador and Guatemala remains constructive, although inflationary pressures warrant attention. In El Salvador, growth accelerated to 5.1% year-over-year in the second quarter of 2026, increasingly supported by investment and double-digit construction growth. While resilient consumption, tourism revenues and renewed progress under the IMF program provide additional buffers despite lower remittances and higher import costs. In Guatemala, growth remained robust at 4.3%, supported by domestic demand, remittances, manufacturing and exports.

However, inflation has risen to 4.7%, while the medium-term outlook increasingly hinges on translating fiscal expansion and the strengthened public-private partnership framework into infrastructure investment. Alongside institutional improvements that could support the country's path toward investment grade. Now please let me turn the presentation to Mauricio, who will present Nequi as an independent entity followed by Grupo Cibest's quarterly performance.

Mauricio Botero Wolff: Thank you, Laura. Please proceed to Slide #7. Nequi was created 10 years ago with the purpose of improving the way people and business interact with money, and since its inception, its success as a powerful and scalable financial inclusion platform has been compelling with a customer base of more than 29 million users in an activity ratio above 80%. And Nequi was launched in 2016, offering a basic marketplace for top-ups and bill payments. Leveraging on the user's transactional data and cash flow dynamics. In 2019, Nequi launched its first credit product, a significant first step towards the financial evolution of individuals without prior credit history.

The pandemic marked a turning point in Nequi history, as it was one of the channels that the government selected to disburse subsidies, eventually driving fast, massive user engagement, expanding by 4.5x its user base in only 3 years. Since then, it has continued enhancing its marketplace and its value proposition has evolved from individuals towards small business cash management solutions and interoperability. Also, it initiated its regional expansion into El Salvador and Guatemala. Please turn to Slide 8. Its business model is built around three core services that foster engagement, generate high transaction volumes and capture a stable, low-cost operational deposits, complemented by a growing financial portfolio, a marketplace, B2B and cross-border solutions.

As of third quarter, 24 million customers are active users, out of which 18 million are monetized. Moreover, 7 out of 10 Colombian adults have a Nequi account and 3.9 million users of Nequi as their only account. 65% of Nequi account holders are not Bancolombia customers and 42% of payments in Bre-B ecosystem come from Nequi. In fact, exponential growth in user engagement and transaction volumes drove operating leverage and cost dilution, enabling Nequi to reach breakeven in late 2025. Please turn to Slide #9. From an accounting perspective, Nequi's stand-alone financials reflect its balance sheet as of September 30, while the income statement captures only 1 month of full operations as the spinoff was executed on September 1.

Thus, in the following slides, we provide a set of administrative financials and performance metrics for the third quarter and previous quarters on a stand-alone basis, intended only for comparative purposes. Deposits closed at COP 6.9 trillion, down 9.5% quarter-over-quarter as balances normalized of the midyear service bonus and up 24% year-over-year. On the other hand, its loan book expanded 12% in the quarter reaching COP 2.5 trillion. Following the spin-off, Grupo Cibest allocated COP 600 billion of capital to Nequi implying a total solvency ratio of 13%. All in all, Nequi initiates this new phase as an independent entity with a robust balance sheet to support scalable growth going forward. Please turn to Slide 10.

Net interest income increased 5.3% in the quarter due to loan expansion and a COP 20 million increase in interest income as a one-off related to the spin-off. Accordingly, NIM reached 18.1%. Absent of the one-off NIM would have been 16.8%. This represent a significant and diversified source of overall income and continued growing at a steady pace during the quarter. The net fee income ratio closed at 22.6%. From a credit loss perspective, provision expense amounted to COP 145 billion, an increase explained by higher loan origination in a one-off related to the transition between former credit model under local GAAP and the current IFRS accounting.

Thus, cost of risk reached 24.6%, which absent of the one-off, would have remained flat at 16.9% and in line with our expectations given the pace of loan growth. Please turn to Slide 11. ARPAC continues to grow while cost to serve continues to decline, such that ARPAC now represents 2.3x CTS demonstrating the strong operating leverage embedded in its business model. All in all, third quarter's net income was COP 33 billion, equivalent to a 23% ROE. Absent of one-offs related to the spin-off, net income would have reached COP 41 billion, which represents an ROE of 28%. Please turn to Slide 12.

Finally, we expect ROE to reach 28% in 2026 and between 28% and 30% in 2027, driven by loan growth that will support margin expansion while provision expenses evolve consistently with portfolio growth. Please turn to Slide 14. Now Grupo Cibest's gross loan portfolio reached COP 274 trillion, increasing 4.3% quarter-over-quarter and 9.7% and year-over-year, which absent of FX, would have been 13.5%, reflecting a strong underlying business dynamic. Commercial loans were the main growth driver, expanding 5.5% during the quarter as per a more constructive business environment in Colombia. Consumer loans also grew at a faster pace, increasing 2% in the quarter, mainly driven by unsecured personal loans and credit cards.

Meanwhile, mortgages maintaining their positive trend, expanding 2.1% over the quarter. Please proceed to Slide 15. When broken down by entity, Bancolombia continued to drive growth supported by commercial loans. The contraction in the consumer portfolio is explained by the spin-off of Nequi, while Nequi continued to show solid origination dynamics, growing 12% during the quarter. Bancoagricola maintained a positive trend, while BAM declined mainly in commercial loans, yet its consumer portfolio is showing signs of recovery with September posting the strongest month-over-month growth of the year. Cross-border lending continued to expand through our offshore operations, allowing us to provide competitive foreign currency financing across different geographies.

As of September, BAM's cross-border loan portfolio grew 63% year-over-year, while Bancoagricola expanded 13%. Please proceed to Slide 16. Total deposits reached COP 275 trillion, growing 1.5% quarter-over-quarter and 8.6% year-over-year. Excluding FX, annual growth would have been 13%. Bancolombia's growth came primarily from time deposits to offset part of the deposit migration resulting from Nequi's spinoff. The decline in savings accounts reflect seasonality related to payroll and employee benefit payments. At Bancoagricola and BAM, deposit growth was mainly driven by sight deposits. Please proceed to Slide 17.

Our funding mix remained resilient, supported by the strength of our sight deposit base, which represents 57% of total funding and provides a structural advantage in containing funding costs in the current interest rate environment. The cost of deposits increased slightly to 4.5%, reflecting Colombia's higher interest rate and the greater share of institutional savings accounts and time deposits. Please proceed to Slide 18. Net interest income reached COP 5.7 Trillion, decreasing 4.9% over the quarter, equivalent to a NIM of 7.4%. The drivers of the quarterly decrease are twofold. First, the normalization of treasury income following an exceptionally strong second quarter.

And second, lending NIM contraction due to higher funding needs related to Nequi's spin-off and to the positive dynamic of the commercial loan portfolio. Bancoagricola and BAM also reported NIM compression, mainly reflecting higher funding costs and lower lending and investment income, respectively. On an annual basis, however, while loans are growing at 9.7%, net interest income is increasing almost 16% and underscoring our robust intermediation capacity. Please proceed to Slide 19. Net fee income reached COP 1.4 trillion, increasing 1.6% over the quarter and 15.5% over the year and remains an important and diversified source of revenues. Fee income growth was broad-based.

However, bancassurance continued to stand out, growing 17% over the year and 3% over the quarter supported by the positive performance of our alliance with SURA. Moreover, fee expenses decreased both during the quarter and during the year, driven by ongoing efficiency initiatives. All in all, fee income ratio stood at 21%. Please proceed to Slide 20. Net provision charges reached COP 1.2 trillion, up 17% over the quarter, mainly reflecting an increase in a specific client segment in Bancolombia as well as the consumer segment, driven by higher originations. BAM recorded higher provisions following updates to its expected loss models, incorporating new information for the year while Bancoagricola's provision expenses remained elevated with higher returns adjusted by risk.

Overall, quarterly cost of risk stood at 1.8% and bringing the 9-month accumulated cost of risk to 1.7%. We continue to closely monitor recent events that could affect asset quality. While proactively managing exposures and addressing potentially affected clients. Starting with the earthquake in Colombia, asset quality in the affected areas remains in line with the overall local loan book, supported by relief measures and proactive client management. We may see some deterioration going forward as collections normalize, and we are building provisions accordingly with no expected impact on our cost of risk guidance range for either this year or next year. Regarding El Nino, our main exposure is concentrated in agribusiness, particularly agro exporters.

Provision expenses related to these exposures have already been recognized in line with expected credit losses. Given our limited exposure to potentially affected clients, we do not expect any material additional impact. Please proceed to Slide 21. Delinquency ratios remained well contained across portfolios during the quarter and reflect a meaningful reduction on a yearly basis. Moreover, from an expected losses perspective, Stage 1 has increased significantly its share, driven by growth on originations while Stage 2 and Stage 3 exposures declined over the year. Coverage remained solid at 131% and for 30-day past due loans in 195% for 90-day past due loans.

Overall, these trends indicate that the asset quality remains in line with our guidance considering the pace of growth. Please proceed to Slide 22. Operating expenses remained broadly stable, increasing only 0.3% quarter-over-quarter, driven by higher financial transaction taxes related to the ordinary and extraordinary dividend payments. On a year-to-date basis, expenses grew 8.7%, mainly reflecting the wealth tax recognized earlier this year. Excluding this effect, annual expense growth would have been approximately 5.2%, that is close to 1 percentage point below inflation. Overall, the consolidated cost-to-income ratio stood at 46.6%. We remain focused on structural efficiency and have launched different initiatives addressing our most significant operating and fee related expenses.

In parallel, our AI program is accelerating its adoption across the organization to enhance productivity, supporting a more scalable operating model. Please turn to Slide 23. Shareholders' equity reached COP 39 trillion, up 1.7% over the quarter. Mainly driven by earnings generation, while the year-over-year decline mainly reflects the Banistmo divestment. In July, Bancolombia issued COP 1 billion intra-group capital instrument contributing 44 basis points as additional Tier 1. Combined with the other intragroup transactions, this enhances the group's capital efficiency while providing additional flexibility to support growth in strategic priorities. Bancolombia's stand-alone solvency ratio remained relatively stable at 13.7% as earnings generation and the AT1 issuance helped offset the extraordinary dividend and growth in risk-weighted assets.

Finally, Cibest stand-alone double leverage increased to 98%, reflecting dividend distributions, yet preserving flexibility for corporate initiatives. Please turn to Slide 24. Net income reached COP 2 trillion, which represents an ROE of 22%. The accumulated net income increased 10.5% over the year despite the absence of Banistmo's earnings contribution. And consistently, ROE has jumped from 18% to 22% in the same period underscoring the rationale behind the divestment and the merits of the capital reallocation strategy. With this, I will now hand the presentation back to Juan Carlos. Juan Carlos?

Juan Uribe: Thank you, Mauricio. Please turn to Slide 26. Turning now to our guidance. For 2026, we are revising our loan growth outlook upwards. From a range of 7% to 8% to a range of 8% to 9%. This reflects stronger demand for commercial loans in Colombia. All other guidance items remain unchanged. For 2027, we project a slightly higher loan growth of 9% to 10%, again, led by commercial loans in Colombia, provided the fiscal deficit narrows in an orderly and gradually way. We also expect NIM of 7.5% to 7.7% and a cost of risk of 1.9% to 2.1%, reflecting stronger origination and interest rates that are likely to remain high.

Finally, we expect an efficiency ratio of 46% to 47%. We remain committed to a cost discipline while continuing to invest in our business transformation. Please turn to Slide 27. To conclude, if macroeconomic conditions to improve and investment confidence rebounds strongly, as we anticipate, Grupo Cibest is uniquely well placed to seize the growth opportunities ahead. And even in a more adverse scenario, our proven NIM management, some credit underwriting, cost discipline and efficient capital allocation allow us to deliver sustainable ROE throughout the economic cycle. With this, we conclude our prepared remarks. We will now be pleased to take your questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] And our first question will come from Ernesto Gabilondo with Bank of America.

Ernesto María Gabilondo Márquez: Thank you. Hi, good morning, Juan Carlos, Mauricio and Catalina, and thanks for the opportunity to ask questions. My first question will be on your earnings growth expectation for next year. So you have mentioned ROE could be maintained between 21% to 22% next year, but just wondering how should we expect in terms of earnings growth? And for my second question is on Nequi. If I am not mistaken, Nequi represents around 2% of Cibest consolidated net income. So how do you see the Nequi contribution to Cibest's earnings in the future? And wondering if you have any plans to IPO this business in the future? Or if we should just consider it as another subsidiary within Cibest.

Juan Uribe: Thank you, Ernesto. Let me take your question regarding Nequi, and I going to ask Mauricio to take your question about earnings. As you mentioned, Nequi today represents around 2% of Grupo Cibest net income. It's still small. Nequi will grow in the future, and we are very optimistic. But the size of Bancolombia is going to continue to be very important in Cibest. So Nequi will gain some importance in the future, probably in 2030 will be something around 8% to 10%. If the growth is strong, particularly on loans and depending on the credit cycle. But Nequi, it's an alternative.

I mean it's a diversification of Grupo Cibest, but Bancolombia will continue to be the most important entity for Grupo Cibest. But Nequi will add diversification, as I mentioned, and alternatives to have presence in the Colombian market. And also it's going to be an avenue of growth in other markets, particularly in Central America. Regarding the -- your question of our IPO, now Nequi is a separate entity fully owned by Grupo Cibest that give us the opportunity to assess different strategic alternatives. We are not thinking about an IPO in the short term.

But with this corporate structure, we have open alternatives, as I mentioned, to develop Nequi and to find the best way to give Nequi those avenues of growth. So we'll continue developing the business in Colombia and in the other markets that we are. And then in parallel, we will be assessing any additional strategic alternatives, but that is not going to happen in the short term is. Now regarding earnings, Mauricio?

Mauricio Botero Wolff: Ernesto, when we think about the end of this year, net income should be around COP 8.5 trillion. And that should be in the upper part of our ROE guidance. And when we think about 2027, the growth should be between 8% and 10% of that net income. So if you think about either COP 9.2 trillion, COP 9.3 trillion, that should give you the 21.5%, 22% ROE guidance that we're thinking for next year.

Operator: Our next question will come from Tito Labarta with Goldman Sachs.

Daer Labarta: Two questions also. I think Juan Carlos, you mentioned as long as that kind of happens gradually. So how do you think about that fiscal adjustment? How do you think -- what are the upside, downside risk to loan growth depending on how that evolves. Also, I guess, on the consumer lending, which has lagged a little bit. Do you think that can accelerate?

Is that maybe more second half of '27 as there's more visibility on the fiscal adjustment. So just to think about the sustainability of the loan growth, given some of the macro risk that are still there for Colombia. And then second question, just on the sustainability of the ROE. More longer term, I know you gave the guidance of 21% to 22% for 2027. But you still have a high rate environment as eventually rates come down with competitive pressure on your NIM. How should we think about what the sustainable ROE should be longer term?

Juan Uribe: Thank you, Tito. Loan growth and what we are seeing is that the demand for commercial loans is strong. This third quarter showed that the demand was there, and there are companies thinking about new projects, projecting 2027 with a more economic activity. So there is demand and we are seeing that on the -- also on the fourth quarter. So we -- even though the rates are high, what companies are thinking that there is an opportunity, particularly in Colombia. Also, they are seeing some opportunities in Venezuela. So they are preparing for that and they are investing and expecting also that the rates will go down by the end of next year.

In terms of consumer lending I am a little less optimistic. I think there is going to be demand, but there is not going to be a strong growth on consumer loans. In the past, consumer loans were growing very aggressively or very strong. And I think that's going to the growth is to moderate in the future due to more -- the rates, the level of the rates and also the fiscal situation. And that open the conversation to what we think is going to be that the fiscal situation. And I'm going to ask Laura to give you some comments about how we see the development of the fiscal situation of Colombia.

Laura Clavijo: Thank you, Juan Carlos. Yes. Indeed, out of fiscal sustainability and adjustment is the talk of the town. Whether it should be accompanied by the IMF apparently a disbursement of around $15,000 -- $15,000 million. As well as the fiscal adjustment, the fiscal adjustment as presented in the whole economic rescue bill is worth 2.4% of GDP -- it's an ambitious number, but our kind of base case scenario more leaned bias towards fiscal adjustment by budget expenditure cuts should give us a base scenario of around COP 30 billion reduction, which would be an adjustment of around 1.4% of GDP.

We believe that this base case scenario accompanied by multilateral support is -- even though it's not sufficient to really bring down the levels of debt moving forward and there they will have to move with some fiscal adjustment later on. It should be sufficient to maintain investor confidence and reduce expenditure in line with 7.9% GDP fiscal deficit for 2027. So these are big numbers in terms of the fiscal adjustment. But I would comment that there is -- there seems to be a consistent message in terms of the importance and the necessity to do this important budget cut really soon.

Mauricio Botero Wolff: And regarding your question about the ROE in the long term. We -- as you know, we have this tailwind that is going to help us in 2027. So that's why we believe the 21% to 22% ROE is feasible. But going forward, when interest rates start coming down, and we reach more stable inflation and interest rate levels along with GDP growth and ROE should be around 20%. Everything that we're doing in terms of operations, in terms of capital structure is targeting the long-term ROE of 20%.

Operator: We'll go next to Yuri Fernandes with JPMorgan.

Yuri Fernandes: Congrats on loan growth revenues. Mauricio Botero Wolff: Yes, we are expecting NIM to increase 10 bps approximately. And that's basically because of the effect of interest rates and sensitivity with NIMs. Just to give you an idea, when we started 2026, interest rates from the Central Bank were at a lower level. So what we have seen throughout the year is an increase in interest rates which helps us in the average, but the average of the year will be lower this year to that one of 2027 because we're going to start 2027 at a higher rate, and we expect that rate to be stable until the fourth quarter of the year. So that explains the expected increase in net interest margin.

Now in terms of cost of risk, the explanation there is we -- we're expecting growth. We are hoping to take advantage of the demand for lending that we're seeing in the commercial segment in the corporate segment. And that's a segment with lower margins that not only has lower yields but also push us in terms of funding to get funding from institutional investors. So that's positive growth, but put some pressure in margins, but the growth itself demands provision.

So most of the increase in cost of risk that we're expecting for 2027 comes from growth, both in commercial loans and in consumer loans in which we tend to go to some risk bracket in which we're not participating. Also, we have to take into account that we have this earthquake just recently, and we have to wait and see the effects of that in the coming couple of years.

And Yuri, let me add that at the beginning of next year, we also will have the effects of El Niño that we foresee that it's going to be strong and it's going to affect particularly in some sectors, agriculture, mainly, but also in Colombia, the effect of El Niño could have some collateral effects on energy supply. So because of that, we have been -- we are conservative on the cost of risk for 2027, Yuri.

Yuri Fernandes: No, super clear. So El Niño, a little bit of the growth. I think that explained a lot on earthquake like on behind the cost of risk. And if I may, just a quick one on Nequi, you're calling for some deposit acceleration. You're growing your users calling for 5%. You are very penetrated, you already have a lot of clients. So basically, what this implies is average balance of deposits growing, right, on a year-over-year like less users, more deposits, more balance.

What is the strategy here for you to grow the average deposit of the Nequi users?

Juan Uribe: Yuri, Nequi is going to reach 30 million clients -- customers soon. Of those, around 24 million are active. They use Nequi on a regular basis. If we take into account that there are 44 million adults in Colombia, that's high percentage of the population are the Nequi users. But we will continue to add products and services to the platform to Nequi that will -- what we have seen is that Nequi will become the main source of financial services for more -- many people, and that will increase the average of deposits that they maintain in Nequi. So Nequi will continue adding services, investment also on other types of loans and that will create that virtuous circle of being Nequi more the -- as I mentioned, the main source of financial services and principality is going to be there on Nequi.

Operator: Our next question comes from Daniel Vaz with Safra.

Daniel Vaz: Congrats on the results. I wanted to ask a question on fees. You don't give guidance for this line. So good to get a sense on the trends. So your net fees are running at about, I think it's COP 1.4 trillion per quarter. And at the margin, you're growing, I think, 15% year-over-year, right? So if you look to 2027 and this breakdown of 15%, I think you're growing mid-single digits on the gross fees and fee expenses that are coming down. So what do you see as sustainable growth for maybe 2027, 2028, since you're getting good traction on the commercial business? And maybe a second question related to fee income ratio. So you reached 21% this quarter.

You got, again, good traction in commercial business in Nequi and you get some efficiency gains to capture going forward. So what's the level of fee income ratio that makes sense for us to model for your long term?

Mauricio Botero Wolff: In terms of fee guidance, what we have seen in 2026 is a very positive result on fee expenses we have been able to contain the fee expense growth. And that way, we have reached the 15% net fee growth. Now for 2027, that is probably not going to be sustainable. So we're going to see revenue on fees growing more in line with the expenses. Both of them should be growing between 10% to 12%. That way, the guidance for net fees for next year should be around 12%. But we will keep on investing on how to transfer the operational processes that demand the fee expenses in order to defend and sustain the margin for fees.

So in a more like longer-term picture in which margins come down, fee income ratio should reach figures closer to 25%, but somewhere between 20% and 25% and is reasonable to project and it will all depend on margins, as I explained before.

Operator: Moving on to Andres Soto with Santander Mexico.

Andres Soto: I have a couple of questions. The first one on your double leverage ratio. You have mentioned the 98% level on this third quarter. What is your expectation by year-end? And what is your assumption both for the 2027 guidance and for your medium-term guidance in this metric?

Mauricio Botero Wolff: Andres, yes, our double leverage ratio is around 98%. As you know, after the divestment of Banistmo, it decreased significantly. We do not believe that's going to be above 105, 110 tops, that's basically because of the way we plan to manage leverage. We have a lot of room for leverage. As we have mentioned before, the 120% is the ratio that the risk rating agencies expected us to have, but thinking about between 100 and 105 for double leverage in 2027 should be -- should work.

Andres Soto: Mauricio, how do you guys think about the combination of cash dividends and buybacks?

Mauricio Botero Wolff: So we think about it in a very different way. Both of them are very important tools to manage the leverage structure and the value creation for shareholders. But the buyback program is executed only on market conditions. So it's a tool. We have it. We look at the market every day, but we are not going to execute unless we believe it's an attractive price to not only execute but also to signal the market.

Whereas ordinary dividend is more a result of the leverage structure we have leaving the operational banks having the solvency ratios that they need to absorb growth and the excess capital flowing into the holding that way being able to distribute between 50% and 60% of our net income. So if you think about ordinary dividends going forward, it should be with a growth of inflation plus 2 or 3 points, growing in real terms. Now extraordinary dividends are only coming with extraordinary milestones as it was the creation of Cibest and the divestment of Banistmo.

Andres Soto: That's very clear. And I have a different question, and this is regarding your loan growth expectations for 2027. You mentioned this is going to be driven by commercial lending, when you see the competitive environment, how do you see the risk-adjusted returns that these new commercial loan production is going to produce versus the one that you currently have in your book?

Mauricio Botero Wolff: Andres, the competitive environment is tough. There is a lot of competition, but we are very well positioned, not only in terms of capital, that we have plenty to absorb big tickets and be able to work with our corporate clients, but also with funding. As you know, we have a competitive advantage in funding, and we are activating that to be able to work with those customers. But also and most important of all, is our customer-centric strategy in which we are not focused on competing on pricing. We're competing more in value proposition.

We're competing more in terms of being the principal relationship of our customers in order to be able to serve them with not only lending needs, but everything related to structuring, advisory in all their financial needs.

Operator: Moving on to Santiago Villanueva with Davivienda Corredores.

Santiago Villanueva Lizcano: I just have two, the first one is, what opportunities do you see for the group in terms of RUGE, the new program through which the government aims to incentive the private investment? And my second question is that I would like to better understand the differences between the year-to-date net income for Nequi as reported during the call and the year-to-date net income through August as reported to the Superintendencia Financiera. While a loss of COP 21 billion is reported to the Superintendencia Financiera the figure mentioned during the call, shows a profit of COP 111 billion. So how should I read those differences?

Juan Uribe: Thank you, Santiago. Regarding the incentives that the government is proposing on its fiscal project that they presented or presented to the Congress, I think it's a good opportunity for Colombia and for investors I think one of the main challenges that Colombia has today, it's the lower rate of investment to GDP. Colombia used to have levels around 24%. Now it's 16%. So the proposed measures, I think, are going to incentivize the investment and the idea, the goal is that, that investment returned to levels of more than 24% of GDP, as I mentioned.

For us, we will need to wait and see how the -- what is the final result and what ends being the decision of Congress regarding those incentives for investment. We think there is going to be an opportunity, but we will make, as I mentioned, wait and see.

Laura Clavijo: I would just add that our growth forecast of 2.4% for 2027 does, in fact, include the positive signals in terms of investments that are already in place. And that would be furthermore boosted by the program such as RUGE. We estimate investments to grow 3.5% in 2026 and 4.7% in 2027. And as Juan Carlos was mentioning that will gradually bring investment as a percentage of GDP, at least for next year, around 17%, 18%. Still a long way to go from our golden years in investment, but definitely signals in the right direction.

Mauricio Botero Wolff: Now in terms of your question about Nequi. So Nequi is very particular and we need to understand the difference between the accounting figures, formal accounting figures and the managerial accounting figures. So it was born in September 1. So it only has in the third quarter, it only has a P&L of 1 month of operation. We have the balance sheet of that was built throughout the history. So the way we presented Nequi assuming it existed from January 1, 2026, and that way managerial net income should be between COP 160 billion or COP 180 billion.

Now for next year, that should grow and be above COP 250 billion, but -- it's important to expect that 2027 figures should converge. So the managerial accounting and the formal accounting is going to look much more similar as we build the history of Nequi going forward.

Operator: We'll hear next from [ Alonso Aramburu ] with BTIG.

Unknown Analyst: There's been discussions about the potential increase in the interest rate cap [Foreign Language]. I'm just wondering if this materializes and let's assume the [Foreign Language] increases by 4 or 5 percentage points. What kind of impact would that have on your NIM in 2027?

Juan Uribe: There have been a lot of discussions, as you mentioned, regarding the cap rate in Colombia. And our view is that in Colombia, there is not just one cap rate. Actually, there are like six for different types of loans. The most common, it's the consumer loans cap that applies for credit cards and consumer loans. But there are other cap rates for different type of loans. As a matter of fact, in Nequi, around 6% of our loans have a cap rate that is different than the consumer cap rates. So there are opportunities today.

Our view is that there will be some conversations on how that rate is calculated but we see difficult to have the discussion in Congress and remove completely the cap rate. So that will give an additional room that conversations about how that cap rate is calculated. And to your question, for us, that's an opportunity. What happened with the cap rate and at the level that is today in Colombia, at least the consumer cap rate which is around 28.4%. It's that generates exclusion to some people that due to their level of risk that cap rate don't allow formal financial institutions to lend them.

If that ceiling increases, probably that will include more people that -- as a matter of fact, are already customers of either Bancolombia or Nequi. So that will allow us to lend them money that today, it's difficult due to the level of risk and the cap rate. So what we see is we can keep operating in the way we're operating today with the current cap rate. But if the calculation of the cap rate changes and allow more room, that will also -- will be a big opportunity for us, Alonso.

Unknown Analyst: Okay. But on a net basis, I would assume your margins should be able to increase marginally, in addition to potentially faster loan growth, right?

Mauricio Botero Wolff: Yes, you are correct.

Operator: This now concludes our question-and-answer session. I would like to turn the floor back over to our CEO, Juan Carlos, for closing comments.

Juan Uribe: Thank you, everybody, for participating in this third quarter conference call results. We are positive about how the Grupo Cibest results are developing. The third quarter showed that we are in the trend of having the results that we were expecting. And what we have seen so far for the fourth quarter, it's positive. So we will think that we will end 2026 in line of what we are expecting. 2027 will have some challenges. But I think we are well prepared to face those challenges and take an opportunity -- advantage of the opportunities that we will have in next year.

With this, we conclude this conference call, and we hope you participate in the fourth quarter conference call results. Thank you very much. Have a good day.

Operator: Ladies and gentlemen, thank you for your participation. This does conclude today's teleconference. You may disconnect your lines, and have a wonderful day.
